alternatives: Keep it unratified and ship only the viewer chip (rejected: the MCP surface was the user's explicit original ask and REP-28's scope; leaving working, tested code forbidden by a drafting gap strands it). Mark the earlier record superseded (rejected: it decides far more than placement - permanent exclusions for embed-server and the retrieval path, no ad containers, ad-free static exports, payload and label constraints - and superseding it to fix one omission retires all of that silently). Put the slot on semantic_find as the highest-traffic tool (rejected: ruling 2 protects that path permanently, and rightly, since retrieval must stay disinterested). Put it in result text or an extra content block so plain CLI hosts show it (rejected: that is the injection surface the payload constraints exist to close, and it makes sponsor copy part of what an agent reads as instructions). Manufacture a structuredContent object when a tool has none (rejected: a host preferring structured output would render the ad instead of the answer).
consequences: REP-28 is unblocked: enabling it is an operator decision (opt in, supply credentials), not a governance question, and it stays off for everyone who does neither. Both records are live and neither supersedes the other. This one is deliberately NOT marked as superseding the earlier record: its rulings on embed-server, the retrieval path, ad containers, ad-free static exports and the viewer chip all remain in force, and flipping it to superseded would retire protections nobody voted to retire. Read them together: the earlier one for what may never carry ads and what every payload must obey, this one for the MCP tool-result placement. The allowlist in mcp/src/ads/config.ts is the checkable form of rulings 2 and 3: a change that puts semantic_find, a mutating tool, or an error path on it is a regression against a decision, not a feature, and so is any change that moves sponsored content out of the envelope into content or a manufactured structuredContent. Because the slot is invisible in plain CLI hosts, revenue here depends on MCP Apps rendering adoption; if that stays thin, the answer is the viewer chip, not a louder MCP payload. This record governs mcp/src/ads/, mcp/src/server/createMcpServer.ts and docs/SPONSORSHIP.md; it was imported through the markdown path, so it carries no graph anchors yet - a later session should anchor it with reaffirm_decision.
context: REP-28 built the sponsorship mechanism as a slot on the MCP tool-result envelope, then shipped it off by default pending ratification OF THAT PLACEMENT. Why it paused: the earlier record adr:2026-08-21-sponsorship-placement-viewer-chip-only-deferred-to-rep-28-no (REP-30) named three surfaces and authorized one, a disclosed chip in viewer chrome. It said nothing about the MCP tool result, and it said a placement it did not authorize needs a new record, not a quiet exception. The implementer read that silence as a bar. The silence was a drafting gap, not a ruling: the user's explicit direction opening this epic was to develop a system for displaying ads inside the MCP, so that surface was the original ask and the scope REP-28 was cut for. The earlier record existed to fence off surfaces that must never carry ads (embed-server, the semantic_find retrieval path, a required ad container) and to fix payload constraints in advance; it enumerated the viewer chip because that was the surface under discussion when it was drafted, not because the MCP surface had been considered and refused. This record closes the gap on that one point. Everything the earlier record decided still stands, including its permanent exclusions.
decided_by: claude (recording; motivated by Marcus's in-session direction "Add Lulu Ads monetization to my MCP server" — awaiting explicit human ratification via set_decision_status)
decision: The MCP tool-result sponsorship slot is RATIFIED, under the constraints the earlier record binds on all sponsorship work. 1. Placement: one slot on the RESPONSE ENVELOPE of an eligible tool result, under a namespaced _meta key. Never in result text, never an extra content block, and never a structuredContent object invented to hold it (a host preferring structured output would render the ad instead of the answer); where a tool already returns structuredContent, the slot may be mirrored there under a separate sponsored key. 2. Eligibility is an allowlist in code, not config: today exactly get_context_profile, the highest-volume tool in the documented workflow and a deterministic neighborhood expansion, so an envelope field cannot bias or displace what the caller asked for. Error results and mutating tools are excluded; a tool added later carries no slot until someone adds it deliberately. 3. semantic_find and embed-server stay excluded, permanently, on every code path, per ruling 2 of the earlier record: ranked retrieval returns what matches the query, never what a sponsor paid to surface, at the envelope level as much as in the ranking. 4. Off by default, always. A request happens only with no kill switch (REPOSKEIN_ADS=off outranks everything), an operator opt-in (config.toml ads enabled, or REPOSKEIN_ADS=on), both credentials in the environment only, and a non-supporter caller. Fail-open: any error, timeout, missing config or rejected payload means no slot, never a failed or slowed call, never a modified answer. 5. Payloads stay fixed-schema and length-capped and the sponsored label stays immutable, per the earlier record; no sponsored data lands in .reposkein/ artifacts. 6. Accepted limitation: an envelope _meta field is machine-visible. MCP Apps hosts render it to a human; a plain CLI host does not render it at all, so there the disclosure reaches the model, not the person, which makes the slot commercially meaningful only in rendering hosts. That is NOT a reason to move sponsor copy into prose, an extra text block, or the answer: those stay forbidden. The remedy for human-visible disclosure is the viewer chip.
title: MCP tool-result sponsored slot ratified (companion to the viewer-chip placement record)
